comparisons.peer_topic: Adoption of ASU 2023-07 on Segment Reporting
comparisons.peer_summary: Citi adopted Accounting Standards Update No. 2023-07, which improves reportable segment disclosures, on a retrospective basis for the annual period ending December 31, 2024, and on a current basis for the interim period beginning January 1, 2025. The adoption includes disclosing significant segment expenses provided to the CODM, the CODM's title and position, and an explanation of how the CODM assesses segment performance.
comparisons.comparison: Both Bank of America and Citi adopted the FASB's ASU No. 2023-07 regarding Segment Reporting on a retrospective basis effective January 1, 2024, to enhance disclosures regarding significant segment expenses provided to the Chief Operating Decision Maker (CODM). Both disclosures highlight that the primary change involves additional reporting on segment expenses rather than a change in financial results.

sentences.text: The Financial Accounting Standards Board amended the segment reporting requirements to add disclosures of incremental segment expense categories.
The Corporation adopted this guidance effective January 1, 2024 on a retrospective basis.

In November 2023, the Financial Accounting Standards Board (FASB) issued Accounting Standards Update (ASU) No. 2023-07, Segment Reporting (Topic 280): Improvements to Reportable Segment Disclosures, intended to improve reportable segments disclosure requirements primarily through enhanced disclosures about significant segment expenses.
Citi adopted the ASU on a retrospective basis for its annual period ending December 31, 2024 and the ASU for the interim period beginning January 1, 2025.

comparisons.peer_topic: Adoption of ASU 2023-07 on Segment Disclosures
comparisons.peer_summary: In January 2024 (interim periods starting January 2025), the firm adopted ASU No. 2023-07 under a retrospective approach, requiring enhanced disclosures about significant segment expenses; adoption had no impact on financial condition, results of operations, or cash flows.
comparisons.comparison: Goldman Sachs and Bank of America both adopted ASU No. 2023-07 on Segment Reporting retrospectively in January 2024. Both disclosures emphasize that the adoption requires enhanced disclosures primarily about significant segment expenses regularly provided to the CODM. Unlike Bank of America, which refers readers to Note 23 for these disclosures, Goldman Sachs explicitly notes that the adoption had no impact on financial condition or results of operations because it only requires additional disclosures.

sentences.text: The Financial Accounting Standards Board amended the segment reporting requirements to add disclosures of incremental segment expense categories.
The Corporation adopted this guidance effective January 1, 2024 on a retrospective basis.
The additional disclosures are included in Note 23 - Business Segment Information.

In November 2023, the FASB issued ASU No. 2023-07, "Improvements to Reportable Segment Disclosures." This ASU requires enhanced disclosures primarily about significant segment expenses that are regularly provided to the chief operating decision maker.
This ASU became effective for the firm for annual periods beginning in January 2024, and is effective for interim periods beginning in January 2025 under a retrospective approach.
Since this ASU only requires additional disclosures, adoption of this ASU did not have an impact on the firm's financial condition, results of operations or cash flows.

comparisons.peer_topic: Adoption of Accounting Standard for Segment Reporting
comparisons.peer_summary: The Firm adopted the accounting standard 'Segment Reporting - Improvements to Reportable Segment Disclosures' retrospectively for the year ended December 31, 2024, which requires additional disclosures on segment expenses and the CODM, without changing the identification of segments or the CODM.
comparisons.comparison: JPMorgan Chase and Bank of America both adopted the 'Segment Reporting - Improvements to Reportable Segment Disclosures' standard retrospectively for the year ended December 31, 2024. Both firms note that this adoption requires additional disclosures primarily relating to significant segment expenses and the CODM. A key similarity is that JPMorgan explicitly states the adoption did not change the identification of its reportable segments or CODM, similar to Bank of America's implication that the change is disclosure-focused rather than structural.

The Corporation adopted this guidance effective January 1, 2024 on a retrospective basis.

Adoption of accounting standard - Segment Reporting - Improvements to Reportable Segment Disclosures: This guidance was adopted retrospectively for the Firm's annual Consolidated Financial Statements for the year ended December 31, 2024.
The adoption of this guidance requires additional reportable segment disclosures, primarily relating to significant segment expenses and the chief operating decision maker ("CODM").
Adoption of this guidance did not result in changes to the identification of the Firm's reportable business segments, or of its CODM.

comparisons.comparison: Morgan Stanley and Bank of America both adopted the 'Segment Reporting - Improvements to Reportable Segment Disclosures' accounting update retrospectively, effective January 1, 2024. Both disclosures indicate that this update requires additional annual and interim reportable segment disclosures, specifically concerning significant segment expenses and items regularly provided to the chief operating decision maker.

sentences.text: The Financial Accounting Standards Board amended the segment reporting requirements to add disclosures of incremental segment expense categories.
The Corporation adopted this guidance effective January 1, 2024 on a retrospective basis.
The Firm adopted the Segment Reporting - Improvements to Reportable Segment Disclosures accounting update retrospectively, effective January 1, 2024.

This accounting update requires additional reportable segment disclosures on an annual and interim basis, primarily about significant segment expenses and other segment items that are regularly provided to the chief operating decision maker and included within the reported measure of segment profit or loss.
